requirements.text: Every entry in the ranked candidate-vehicle list carries a decision margin: its score minus the score of the next-lower-ranked candidate in the same cluster's list, and, for the lowest-ranked candidate, its score minus the abstention floor (CORE-286). The margin is recorded as a numeric field on the DATA-OUT-300 record alongside the score.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-280 (CORE-280): Input: a document set constructed to produce one cluster with four candidate vehicles scored 0.810, 0.790, 0.520 and 0.510, run with the abstention floor F = 0.400. Expected: the four candidate records carry decision_margin values 0.020, 0.270, 0.010 and 0.110 respectively (each within 1e-9 of the stated value), in the same rank order as the score field.
requirements.rationale: The need statement asks the recommender to act differently when the distribution is flat. "Flat" is only actionable if it is measured, and the margin between adjacent ranks is the measurement the rest of this block consumes. It is also the confidence figure a reviewer reads to know how much weight the top-1 answer can bear: a top-1 at 0.81 with a 0.20 margin and a top-1 at 0.81 with a 0.002 margin are different claims, and today's output cannot tell them apart. Recording it also satisfies references/ai-boundaries.md rule 3 (the record must be reconstructable) for the grey-area cases specifically.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: a named numeric field exists on each candidate record and equals a stated arithmetic difference. It does not assert how the margin is used, displayed, or thresholded - those are CORE-281, CORE-282 and CORE-288.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "Output record" (every recommendation traces to a row or span); references/ai-boundaries.md operating rule 3.

requirements.text: For each cluster, the pipeline records a tie group: the highest-ranked candidate plus every lower-ranked candidate whose score falls within the documented near-tie epsilon (ε) of the highest score. The tie group is recorded on the cluster's result record in every case, including when it has exactly one member.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-281 (CORE-281): Input: ε = 0.020 and a document set constructed to produce one cluster with four candidate vehicles scored 0.810 (V-A), 0.795 (V-B), 0.792 (V-C) and 0.640 (V-D). Expected: the cluster's result record carries a tie group of exactly three members - V-A, V-B, V-C in rank order (0.810-0.795 = 0.015 <= ε; 0.810-0.792 = 0.018 <= ε; 0.810-0.640 = 0.170 > ε) - and V-D is absent from it.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: membership of a named set is exactly the candidates within ε of the top score. The value of ε, how the group is then ordered, and how it is displayed are separate requirements (CORE-282, CORE-288).
requirements.rationale: This is the direct operationalization of "when the probabilities distribution is flat." Measuring only the rank-1/rank-2 gap misses the case the client described - three or four candidates on a plateau - so the detector is defined over the whole top of the distribution, not over an adjacent pair. Anchoring the group to the top score rather than chaining adjacent margins keeps it from growing transitively down a long gentle slope, which would sweep genuinely worse candidates into a tie.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/challenge-brief.md (the rubric scores the top-5 list, so the plateau that matters is the one at the top); references/vehicle-matching.md, "Scoring a cluster against vehicles".

requirements.text: Candidates inside a tie group are ordered by a fixed, documented sequence of tie-break keys applied in a fixed order, and each candidate's result record names the single key that placed it below the candidate immediately above it.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-282 (CORE-282): Input: the tie-break ladder configured as (1) NMCARS 5237.102 mandatory-consideration prior, (2) office affinity P(vehicle | awarding office code) from the vendored order history, (3) ordering-period headroom in days against the cluster's stated period of performance, (4) friction rank per the vehicle taxonomy in references/far-consolidation-rules.md, (5) ordinal comparison on vehicle_id. A cluster is constructed producing a three-member tie group V-A, V-B, V-C all scored 0.700, none of them Annex 22-eligible (key 1 neutral for all three), with office affinity V-A = 0.42, V-B = 0.42, V-C = 0.11, and ordering-period headroom V-A = 1200 days, V-B = 400 days. Expected: the tie group is ordered V-A, V-B, V-C; V-B's record names "ordering-period-headroom" as the key placing it below V-A; V-C's record names "office-affinity" as the key placing it below V-B.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: the deciding key for each adjacent pair inside a tie group is both determined by a fixed ordered ladder and named in the output. Which keys the ladder contains is set by CORE-284 (rung 1) and by the algorithm documentation; that the ladder is exhaustive is CORE-283.
requirements.rationale: This is the "which way should the recommender go" half of the need statement, made auditable. An unnamed tie-break is indistinguishable to a reviewer from an arbitrary one, and a Demo Day question about why one vehicle outranked another cannot be answered from a score alone (references/vehicle-matching.md: "a bare score cannot be defended in a determination or a debrief"). Naming the deciding key also keeps the tool on the assembling side of the line in references/ai-boundaries.md - it discloses the rule it applied rather than asserting a conclusion.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "Policy priors" row and "Output record"; references/far-consolidation-rules.md, "Vehicle taxonomy by friction, lowest first".

requirements.text: The tie-break ladder terminates in a total order: after the final key is applied, no two candidates in a tie group compare equal, and the resulting order is independent of input file enumeration order.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-283 (CORE-283): Input: a document set constructed so that two candidate vehicles V-P and V-Q are identical on every tie-break key - same score (0.700 to within 1e-12), same modal PSC and NAICS, same awarding office code, same office-affinity value, same ordering-period headroom, same friction rank - and differ only in vehicle_id. Run the full pipeline 20 times, shuffling the input directory's file enumeration order before each run. Expected: V-P precedes V-Q in the ranked list in all 20 of 20 runs (ordinal comparison on vehicle_id), with no run producing the reverse order.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: the ladder leaves no pair unresolved. Separate from CORE-282, which a reviewer could satisfy with a ladder that names keys but still bottoms out in an equality - exactly the reproducibility failure this item forbids.
requirements.rationale: CORE-210 requires the same top-5 in >=95% of runs but says nothing about the mechanism; an unbroken tie resolved by dictionary or filesystem enumeration order is the most likely way that bar is silently lost once vehicle matching is added. The existing VehicleRecommender.cs already ends its comparator on an ordinal vehicle_id sort for exactly this reason, so this requirement turns an undocumented implementation convention into a stated, tested obligation that also covers the new policy-prior ladder.
requirements.source_citation: Challenge critical technical criteria, "produces same top 5 results 95% of the time" (references/challenge-brief.md); references/vehicle-matching.md, "Deterministic means deterministic" (break ties explicitly).

requirements.text: When a tie group contains SeaPort-NxG and the cluster's requirement content is classified as Annex 22 functional-area services with no recorded NMCARS 5237.102 exception (FAR 6.302 action, below the simplified acquisition threshold, 8(a) set-aside, FAR Part 12 or FAR 8.4 commercial, or FAR Part 13 simplified), SeaPort-NxG is placed first within that tie group.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-284 (CORE-284): Input, cluster X: a PWS for in-service engineering support (Annex 22 functional area), no SF 1449, no set-aside marking, estimated value $14M, producing a tie group of SeaPort-NxG at 0.712 and a NAWCAD Pax MAC at 0.705 with ε = 0.020. Expected: SeaPort-NxG is ranked first in cluster X's tie group and its record names the deciding key as the NMCARS 5237.102 mandatory-consideration prior, citing that section by number. Repeat with cluster Y: an SF 1449 commercial services RFQ under FAR Part 12, estimated value $180K, producing a tie group of SeaPort-NxG at 0.680 and GSA MAS at 0.674. Expected: cluster Y's rung-1 evaluation is recorded as not applicable with the reason "FAR Part 12 commercial - NMCARS 5237.102 exception", and the prior does not place SeaPort-NxG first.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: a stated precondition produces a stated ordering inside the tie group. The exception list is part of the precondition, not a second behavior - the negative branch in the test procedure exercises the same single conditional, not an additional one.
requirements.rationale: The need statement says the grey-area call should come from "understanding of the need" - for Navy services, the governing understanding is a rule, not a preference: NMCARS 5237.102 makes SeaPort consideration mandatory for Annex 22 work. A recommender that ranks a NAWCAD MAC over SeaPort-NxG on a hundredth of a similarity point, for work SeaPort must be considered for, is wrong in a way a NAVAIR reviewer will spot immediately. Encoding it as a named, cited rung rather than as score weight keeps it auditable and keeps it from distorting the score channels. The exception list is carried in full because applying the prior to a Part 12 commercial RFQ would be equally wrong in the other direction.
requirements.source_citation: NMCARS 5237.102 (mandatory consideration, Annex 22); exception list confirmed against the DON Best Practices Handbook for Services Acquisitions FY2024, per .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/far-consolidation-rules.md, "Navy approvals (NMCARS)"; NMCARS 5237.103 (waiver D&F to DASN(P)).

requirements.text: No candidate vehicle that failed a hard constraint check appears in a tie group or at any rank in the candidate list; tie-break keys are applied only over candidates that passed every hard constraint check.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-285 (CORE-285): Input: a cluster whose stated period of performance begins 2027-01-01, with ε = 0.050 and two scoring candidates - V-OPEN at 0.710 whose vendored ordering-period end is 2031-01-01, and V-CLOSED at 0.730 whose vendored ordering-period end is 2025-09-30. Expected: the ranked candidate list contains V-OPEN at rank 1 and does not contain V-CLOSED at any rank, and the recorded tie group has exactly one member (V-OPEN), despite V-CLOSED holding the higher raw score and the two scores falling within ε of each other.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion, stated as an exclusion: constraint-failed candidates are absent from the tie group and the ranked list. It deliberately does not assert that the constraint check runs, what checks exist, or that eliminated candidates are logged with a reason - those belong to the vehicle knowledge-base and constraint-check requirements proposed under the vehicle-resources need statement.
requirements.rationale: A tie-break is the exact place a dead vehicle gets resurrected: its score is within ε of the winner, so a policy prior or an affinity figure can promote it to rank 1. references/vehicle-matching.md is explicit that a failed constraint removes a vehicle rather than lowering its score, and this item makes that survive the grey-area path specifically. Recommending a vehicle whose ordering period closes before the requirement's period of performance is not a near-miss, it is an unusable answer - under FAR 16.505(b) there is no order to place.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "Hard constraints" row ("A failed constraint removes the vehicle, it does not lower a score"); FAR 16.505(b); FAR 17.5 and DFARS 217.770 for non-DoD vehicle eligibility.

requirements.text: When no candidate vehicle for a cluster reaches the documented abstention floor F, the cluster's candidate list is emitted empty and the cluster is recorded as a no-vehicle-match result carrying its highest observed candidate score and the value of F.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-286 (CORE-286): Input: F = 0.300 and a three-document cluster constructed so that its best-scoring candidate vehicle reaches 0.210. Expected: the run manifest contains zero candidate-vehicle entries for that cluster, and exactly one no-vehicle-match record for it with highest_observed_score = 0.210 and abstention_floor = 0.300; the run still exits 0 and still produces the OUT-440 bundle.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: below F, the candidate list for that cluster is empty and is replaced by a single named record with two stated fields. The substitution is one behavior with one observable state - there is no way to satisfy half of it.
requirements.rationale: The need statement's grey area has a floor as well as a plateau. When every vehicle scores badly, ranking them anyway manufactures a recommendation out of noise, which is the "model invents the rationale" failure references/ai-boundaries.md warns against, and it is the failure mode that produced NAADAP's earlier precision@5 measuring filename order. Abstaining explicitly, with the observed score and the floor on the record, tells the human decider the difference between "nothing fits" and "the tool did not look."
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/ai-boundaries.md, "The line" and operating rule 2; references/vehicle-matching.md, "never let a one-document cluster outrank a multi-document one by convention".

requirements.text: A cluster recorded as no-vehicle-match (CORE-286) with three or more member documents emits a new-strategic-vehicle-indicated record describing the proposed vehicle in acquisition terms: a scope statement quoting at least one member task statement, the modal PSC and NAICS of its members, the contracting office codes of its members, and a proposed vehicle type.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-287 (CORE-287): Input: F = 0.300 and a four-document cluster of flight-line engineering PWSs drawn from three distinct contracting office codes (N00421, N68335, N61340), constructed so that its best existing-vehicle score is 0.180. Expected: exactly one new-strategic-vehicle-indicated record is emitted for that cluster, carrying a non-empty scope statement that quotes at least one verbatim "shall" statement from a member document, modal PSC R425, modal NAICS 541330, the three office codes listed above, and a proposed vehicle type of "multiple-award IDIQ".
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: a stated precondition produces one record with a stated field set. Following DATA-IN-100's precedent, a normalized record with named required fields is treated as a single verifiable item rather than one requirement per field.
requirements.rationale: The challenge problem statement asks for "consolidating similar requirements into larger vehicles or identifying new strategic contracting vehicles based on future capabilities." Without this path an abstention (CORE-286) is a dead end and the second half of the sponsor's own ask goes unanswered. The member-count floor of three is what separates "no home on an existing vehicle" from "a population large enough to justify standing one up" - the sponsor's own definition of a strategic vehicle is one that lets "a large amount of requirement owners" order under it. Expressing the output in PSC, NAICS, office code and vehicle type is what makes it a recommendation a NAVAIR reviewer can act on rather than a cluster label.
requirements.source_citation: Challenge problem statement, verbatim, per .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/challenge-brief.md, "What the sponsor actually wants"; DoDI 5000.74 Seven Steps, Step 3 Market Research ("whether or not any existing contract vehicles are available to execute the requirement"); references/vehicle-matching.md, "Speak the sponsor's vocabulary".

requirements.text: Every tie group with more than one member and every no-vehicle-match cluster appears in OUT-410's results visualization as a flagged item listing each competing candidate together with the per-channel evidence values that produced its score.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-288 (CORE-288): Input: the N=20 reference set with ε = 0.020 and F = 0.300, tuned so the run produces at least one tie group of two or more members and at least one no-vehicle-match cluster. Expected: OUT-410's results visualization artifact contains a flagged section in which each multi-member tie group lists every competing candidate with its lexical, code-intersection, office-affinity and historical-order channel values, and each no-vehicle-match cluster is listed with its highest observed score; no multi-member tie group or no-vehicle-match cluster present in the manifest is absent from that section.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: a defined set of items appears in one named artifact with a defined per-item content. It asserts presence and completeness of the flagged set, not layout, legibility, or the machine-readable record's shape (CORE-280 to CORE-286).
requirements.rationale: A grey-area call that is only visible by reading the JSON has been silently resolved as far as the human decider is concerned. The need statement's judgement call is only defensible if the competing evidence reaches the person who owns the decision, side by side, at the moment the tool says the answer was close. This is also the Demo Day surface: the judges pick five candidates by hand and ask why, and the flagged section is where that answer lives.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/ai-boundaries.md ("Present reserved decisions as numbered items with owner, evidence for and against, options, and open questions"); references/vehicle-matching.md, "Every recommendation carries its evidence".

requirements.text: No field in any run output states a commerciality, set-aside, contract-type, competition, consolidation or bundling, responsibility, or price-reasonableness conclusion in the Government's voice; a near-tie or tie-break item is expressed only as competing evidence with its deciding key named.
requirements.test_procedure: TP-289 (CORE-289) - Inspection: review the run manifest, OUT-410's results visualization, and the new-strategic-vehicle-indicated records from a full N=20 run against the reserved-decision list in references/ai-boundaries.md, including a literal scan for the determination phrases "is commercial", "shall be set aside", "necessary and justified", "fair and reasonable", "is responsible", "is a responsible source" and "shall be awarded". Expected: zero occurrences of any such phrase asserted as a finding about the requirement or a vendor, and every tie-break item instead reading as a ranked pair of candidates with its deciding key named per CORE-282.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion, stated as a prohibition over the output surface, verifiable by a single inspection pass against one enumerated list. The positive presentation form (owner, options, open questions) is carried by CORE-288 and the algorithm documentation, not asserted here.
requirements.rationale: Tie-breaking is where the tool comes closest to crossing the line, because breaking a tie with NMCARS 5237.102 or a friction rank looks like the beginning of a consolidation determination. FAR 7.107 places that determination with a named human - NMCARS 5207.107-2 puts it at DASN(P) or the HCA - and references/ai-boundaries.md's test is whether the signer could defend every evaluative claim without pointing at the tool. Ranking evidence and disclosing the rule applied passes that test; writing the conclusion does not. This item is also the audit hook that keeps the optional LLM summarization step (CORE-250) from drafting determination language into the bundle.
requirements.source_citation: FAR 7.107-2 and 7.107-3; NMCARS 5207.107-2 (DASN(P)/HCA approval); FAR 1.601 through 1.602-1 (only the CO signs determinations); .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/ai-boundaries.md, "Reserved decisions this skill never originates".

derive.coverage_note:
Three parts of this need statement are already covered and are not restated above.

1. The determinism OUTCOME is CORE-210's - "the same top-5 candidate contract-vehicle list in >=95% of runs." I have not re-asserted reproducibility. CORE-283 refines CORE-210 by requiring the MECHANISM that makes it hold once policy-prior tie-breaking is added: CORE-210 says the answer must be stable, CORE-283 says no pair may be left for the filesystem or a dictionary to order. TP-283 deliberately reuses TP-210's 20-run shape.

2. Reporting a numeric confidence per candidate is already DATA-OUT-300's ("each candidate carrying a numeric confidence/score and the set of source documents that contributed to it"), and exists in code as CandidateVehicle.Score. CORE-280 does not restate that; it refines DATA-OUT-300 by adding the margin, which is the figure the flat-distribution case actually needs and which a bare score cannot express.

3. Producing a results visualization is already OUT-410's, and the bundle is already OUT-440's. CORE-288 proposes no new artifact; it refines OUT-410 by naming content that artifact must carry - the flagged near-tie and abstention items. If the SE prefers, CORE-288 could be folded into OUT-410 as an amendment rather than carried as a new row.

Partially covered in code but in no RTVM row: VehicleRecommender.cs already implements an explicit three-key tie-break (score, then contributing-document count, then ordinal VehicleId) with an inline comment citing CORE-210. That is the ladder CORE-282 and CORE-283 formalize and extend. It is an undocumented implementation convention today, traceable to no requirement, which is exactly the gap this block closes.

Not covered anywhere, in the RTVM or in the code: near-tie detection, policy-prior tie-breaking, abstention, and the new-strategic-vehicle-indicated path. There is no vehicle knowledge base in the codebase at all, so CORE-284, CORE-285 and CORE-287 describe behavior over data that does not yet exist.
derive.tensions:
1. THE SINGLETON 1.0 CONVENTION BLOCKS VERIFICATION OF THIS WHOLE BLOCK. VehicleRecommender.ComputeCohesion returns 1.0 for any one-document cluster "by convention." On the real reference set, 11 of 20 documents were singletons, so today's ranked list opens with a plateau of eleven candidates at exactly 1.0 - an artificial tie group that CORE-281 would flag as the flattest possible distribution while being a pure scoring artifact. Near-tie detection cannot be meaningfully tested, and epsilon cannot be tuned, against a score column containing a spike of exact 1.0s. This block depends on that repair; the repair itself belongs to the scoring requirement, not here.

2. CORE-286 COSTS POINTS UNDER THE PUBLISHED RUBRIC. The challenge awards 2 points per correct prediction against PGIL's list of 20 and states no penalty for a wrong one. Under that scoring, abstaining has strictly negative expected value and guessing is free. The client should see this plainly: defensibility (references/ai-boundaries.md) and score (SN-1) point in opposite directions. Recommended resolution is to keep the abstention record but still emit the sub-floor candidates in a clearly separated "below evidence floor" section, so no scoreable prediction is discarded and no unsupported answer is presented as a recommendation. If the client prefers to maximize score, CORE-286 must be rewritten as a LABELLING requirement rather than a SUPPRESSION requirement - that is a client decision, not an engineering one.

3. CORE-284's SEAPORT PRIOR MAY LOWER MEASURED PRECISION WHILE BEING MORE DEFENSIBLE. Two audits of the reference set on 2026-09-04 found that no document in it was issued by a NAVAIR office and that neither of the two vehicles named in the corpus appeared in the ground-truth set. If PGIL's list of 20 does not reflect NMCARS 5237.102 the way a Navy services SME would, hard-wiring the prior moves candidates away from the scored answers. It should therefore be a configurable, documented rung whose effect is measured both ways in the CORE-260 comparison, not a compiled-in constant. CORE-284 also presumes an Annex 22 functional-area classification the pipeline cannot produce today: DocumentTypeClassifier.cs recognizes five categories by literal token match and otherwise returns Unknown, and IngestionRunner.cs builds each DocumentRecord from four fields only - no PSC, NAICS, contract number, office code or section structure is extracted at all.

4. CORE-284, CORE-285 AND CORE-287 REQUIRE A VEHICLE KNOWLEDGE BASE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. Ordering-period ends, Annex 22 scope text, office-affinity distributions from historical orders, and ceiling headroom must all sit inside the image under NFR-500 with no run-time network under NFR-510. That data pulls against CORE-220's 1-core/2GB/30-minute budget and against the image size DELIV-930's first-time evaluator has to build and pull. None of these three items is verifiable before that knowledge base lands; sequence them behind it.

5. TWO NEW TUNING CONSTANTS INHERIT A KNOWN FAILURE MODE. Epsilon (CORE-281) and F (CORE-286) are exactly the kind of constant that produced the 0.35 similarity threshold - derived from a synthetic ten-document fixture and wrong on real documents, where it left 11 of 20 solicitations as singletons. Both must be derived on the N=20 reference set and re-derived on GFI the day it arrives, with the derivation written into the algorithm documentation the way TfIdfCosineClusteringComponent documents 0.35 today (DELIV-970).

6. CORE-289 SITS AGAINST THE CHALLENGE'S OWN WORD "RECOMMENDATIONS." A reviewer can reasonably read a ranked list of vehicles as an originated recommendation, which is what the rubric asks for and what references/ai-boundaries.md constrains. The line drawn here is that the tool ranks evidence and names the rule it applied, and never writes the FAR 7.107 determination or asserts commerciality, set-aside or contract type. State that line explicitly in the submitted algorithm documentation, because a judge who does not see it stated may read CORE-289's caution as the tool declining to answer the question it was built for.

7. THE CORE-280..289 BAND IS FULLY CONSUMED by these ten items. Any further grey-area requirement - a per-cluster confidence-calibration item, or a separate requirement to log eliminated candidates with the check each one failed - needs a CORE-290+ block.

requirements.text: The vehicle knowledge base ships inside the container image as a single versioned artifact: one root directory containing a `kb_version` identifier string and a `manifest.sha256` file carrying a SHA-256 digest for every file under that root, with no file under the root absent from the manifest.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-600** (KB-600) — Inspection: build the image and list the knowledge-base root (`/app/kb`). Expected: exactly one `kb_version` file whose contents are a single version string (e.g. `2026.09.1`); one `manifest.sha256`; the number of digest lines in `manifest.sha256` equals the number of regular files under the root excluding `manifest.sha256` itself (e.g. 31 records + 3 index files = 34 lines, 34 files); no file under the root is unlisted.
requirements.rationale: "Compartmentalized" means the SME knowledge is a self-contained artifact under configuration control, not a service call and not loose files. A version string plus a complete digest manifest is the minimum shape that lets KB-630 verify integrity and CORE-275 stamp a run. NFR-500 already forbids fetching it at run time; this states what the vendored artifact must be, which NFR-500 does not.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: the artifact is completely manifested and version-identified. Verifying it requires only listing the image's KB root and counting; it asserts nothing about the records' contents (KB-610), their provenance (KB-620), or runtime behavior (KB-630).
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "Building the vehicle knowledge base" ("Version it, hash it, and ship it in the image"); references/ai-boundaries.md operating rule 3.

requirements.text: Every vehicle record in the knowledge base carries a non-empty value for each required field: `vehicle_id`, `name`, `family`, base IDV PIID(s), scope narrative text in the vehicle's own words, `ordering_period_end`, ceiling value, eligible ordering activities, PSC set, NAICS set, socioeconomic pool(s), and `acquisition_path_tier`.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-610** (KB-610): Input: the shipped knowledge-base artifact at `kb_version` 2026.09.1. Run the schema validator over every vehicle record. Expected: zero records report a missing or empty required field; spot-check the SeaPort-NxG record and confirm `ordering_period_end` = 2029-01-01, `eligible_ordering_activities` = "DON only", `family` = "MAC IDIQ", and `acquisition_path_tier` = 1.
requirements.rationale: These twelve fields are exactly the facts a NAVAIR contracting professional uses to answer "could this requirement ride this vehicle": what the vehicle covers, whether it is still orderable, who may order, and which codes and pools it holds. Without all twelve present on every record, the matching channels in CORE-271 and the constraint checks in CORE-272 have nothing to read. Nothing in the codebase holds any of them today — there is no vehicle knowledge base anywhere in `src/`.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: schema completeness across all records, verified by one validator pass with one pass/fail output. It says nothing about where the values came from (KB-620) or whether they are still correct as of a given date.
requirements.source_citation: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "Building the vehicle knowledge base" field list; FAR 16.505(b) (fair opportunity applies only within a vehicle's scope and ordering period).

requirements.text: Every field value in every vehicle record carries a provenance triple recorded alongside the value: source identifier (URL or document title), retrieval date, and SHA-256 of the retrieved source.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-620** (KB-620) — Inspection: draw 10 vehicle records from the shipped artifact and inspect every field value on each. Expected: each value carries `{source, retrieved_on, source_sha256}`; e.g. SeaPort-NxG's `ordering_period_end` shows source = the USAspending IDV award record for the SeaPort-NxG base IDV, `retrieved_on` = 2026-09-04, and a 64-hex-character `source_sha256`; zero of the 10 records contain a field value with a missing, empty, or placeholder provenance element.
requirements.rationale: The knowledge base is the captured SME judgment; a Government evaluator has to be able to check it the way they would check a market-research file. FAR 10.002(e) requires market-research results to be documented in a form the file can carry, and the agent's own boundary rule is that the record must be reconstructable. A vehicle fact with no source is indistinguishable from an invented one, which is the failure mode ai-boundaries.md names explicitly (never fabricate a vehicle name, clause number, or threshold).
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: every value is sourced. Independently satisfiable or violable without KB-610 — a record can hold all twelve fields with no provenance, or carry provenance on a partial field set — so it cannot be folded into KB-610.

requirements.text: Before the vehicle-matching step reads any knowledge-base file, the pipeline recomputes each file's SHA-256 against KB-600's manifest and, on any mismatch, terminates with a non-zero exit code naming the mismatched file and writes no candidate list.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-630** (KB-630): Input: the N=20 reference set and a built image in which one byte of one vehicle record file (`kb/vehicles/seaport-nxg.json`) has been altered after the manifest was written. Run the pipeline. Expected: exit code is non-zero; stderr names `kb/vehicles/seaport-nxg.json` with the expected and computed digests; the output directory contains no candidate list. Re-run against the unaltered image: exit code 0, candidate list produced.
requirements.rationale: A compartmentalized knowledge artifact is only trustworthy if tampering or a partial image layer is detected rather than silently matched against. Failing closed, rather than recommending vehicles from an unverified table, is the only behavior defensible to an IL4 accreditor and to a judge asking what the tool did when its inputs were wrong.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion with one observable failure mode: mismatch halts the run. Verified by a single test with a tampered file and one expected output (non-zero exit, named file, no candidate list). KB-600 is verified by inspection of the image and asserts nothing about runtime behavior, so the two require different methods and must be separate.

requirements.text: Every entry in the ranked candidate list identifies either a `vehicle_id` present in the shipped knowledge base or the reserved literal `NEW-VEHICLE-INDICATED`; no entry's identifier is derived from cluster term text.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-270** (CORE-270): Input: the N=20 reference set with knowledge base `2026.09.1`. Expected: each of the 5 top candidate entries' `vehicle_id` is either an exact key in the knowledge base's vehicle index (e.g. `seaport-nxg`, `nawctsd-tsc-iv`) or the literal `NEW-VEHICLE-INDICATED`; zero entries match the legacy slug pattern `^CLUSTER-\d+-[A-Z0-9-]+$`.
requirements.rationale: The judges score membership in PGIL's predetermined list of 20 vehicles, at 2 points per correct prediction. A cluster labeled by its top TF-IDF terms cannot be scored against that list at all. Today `VehicleRecommender.BuildVehicleId` emits exactly such a slug (`CLUSTER-0001-FLIGHT-LINE-ENGINEERING`) and `CandidateVehicle`'s own documentation states it is "not a lookup against a real-world contract-vehicle name/database" — so the pipeline currently cannot score a single point on SN-1's 2-points-per-correct-prediction criterion. The `NEW-VEHICLE-INDICATED` alternative is required because the challenge's problem is partly about requirements with no home on any existing strategic vehicle; the tool must be able to say so explicitly rather than force a wrong name.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion about the identifier's domain: it is a knowledge-base key or one reserved literal. Testable by set membership with one pass/fail. It asserts nothing about the ordering of the list (CORE-273), the evidence behind an entry (CORE-271), or which vehicles were excluded (CORE-272).

requirements.text: Each candidate vehicle carries one evidence record per matching channel — lexical scope overlap, PSC/NAICS intersection, office affinity, historical orders, hard constraints — and each evidence record holds that channel's score together with at least one traceable identifier for the evidence that produced it: a knowledge-base row id, or a (source filename, section path, sentence) document span.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-271** (CORE-271): Input: a 3-document cluster of flight-line engineering PWSs drawn from the reference set, against knowledge base `2026.09.1`. Expected: the SeaPort-NxG candidate carries five evidence records keyed `lexical`, `codes`, `office_affinity`, `history`, `constraints`; each carries a numeric score; the `lexical` record cites at least one SeaPort-NxG scope sentence by knowledge-base row id and at least one document span as (source filename, section path, sentence); zero of the five records has an empty identifier list.
requirements.rationale: This is the "more than a retrieval service" assertion made verifiable. A bare score cannot be defended in a consolidation determination, at a debrief, or in a Demo Day question; per-channel evidence tied to a row or a span can. It is also the difference between a document pointer and an acquisition judgment: the channels are the six questions an SME actually asks, encoded separately so a reviewer can disagree with one channel without discarding the recommendation. Today `CandidateVehicle` carries a single cohesion number and a filename list and nothing else.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: every channel record is both scored and sourced. Verified by one structural check over one candidate with a single pass/fail. Splitting "scored" from "sourced" would create two rows that can only ever be tested by the same fixture and the same traversal; the failure a reviewer must be able to catch is an unsourced channel, which this states directly.

requirements.text: A vehicle that fails any hard constraint — ordering period ending before the requirement's period-of-performance start, requesting office not an eligible ordering activity, or socioeconomic pool incompatible with the stated set-aside — is absent from the ranked candidate list rather than ranked lower, and the run's eliminations record names the vehicle and the constraint that removed it.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-272** (CORE-272): Input: a 3-document cluster of NAVAIR PMA program-management-support documents with period of performance beginning 2027-01-01 and requesting office N00421, against a knowledge base containing NAVAIR PM CSS MAC (`ordering_period_end` 2023-06-30) and NAWCAD SCI MAC (`ordering_period_end` 2030-03-31), both of which score above threshold on lexical scope overlap. Expected: the ranked candidate list contains `nawcad-sci-mac` and does not contain `navair-pm-css-mac` at any rank; the run's eliminations record contains one row naming `navair-pm-css-mac` with reason "ordering period ended 2023-06-30, before period of performance start 2027-01-01".
requirements.rationale: An unorderable vehicle is not a lesser recommendation, it is a wrong one — there is no fair-opportunity process under FAR 16.505(b) for a closed ordering period, and an ineligible office cannot place the order at all. Scoring such a vehicle lower still lets it displace a correct candidate out of the top 5 that the judges score. Recording the elimination keeps the removal auditable, so a contracting officer who believes a waiver or an extension exists can see exactly which fact to challenge.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion about the disposition of a constraint failure: elimination, not demotion. The eliminations record is the acceptance evidence for that single assertion, not a second behavior — the test cannot distinguish elimination from a very low rank without it.

requirements.text: Where two candidate vehicles' composite scores differ by 0.05 or less, the candidate with the lower `acquisition_path_tier` is ranked first; tier is the fixed five-value acquisition-path taxonomy carried on every candidate with its governing citation — 1 order under an existing in-scope agency MAC (FAR 16.505(b)); 2 FSS/MAS order or BPA call (FAR 8.405); 3 GWAC or other-agency vehicle order (FAR 17.500, DFARS 217.770); 4 new IDIQ (FAR 16.504(c)); 5 new stand-alone contract.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-273** (CORE-273): Input: a cluster whose composite channel scores are GSA MAS 0.73 (`acquisition_path_tier` 2) and SeaPort-NxG 0.71 (`acquisition_path_tier` 1), a difference of 0.02. Expected: `seaport-nxg` is at rank 1 and `gsa-mas` at rank 2; each entry shows its `acquisition_path_tier` and citation (1 / FAR 16.505(b); 2 / FAR 8.405). Re-run with GSA MAS at 0.80 and SeaPort-NxG at 0.71 (difference 0.09): `gsa-mas` is at rank 1, confirming the tie-break applies only inside the 0.05 band.
requirements.rationale: This is "shortest path to fulfillment" made operative rather than decorative. The friction ordering is not a preference — each step down the taxonomy adds a real procedural burden: a synopsis under FAR 5.202(a)(6) is not required for a fair-opportunity order but is for a new stand-alone contract, a single-award IDIQ over $150M needs an SPE D&F under FAR 16.504(c), and a new stand-alone contract needs its own FAR 7.107 determination. When the content evidence cannot separate two vehicles, the one that gets the requirement on contract soonest is the correct answer, and the exposed tier tells a NAVAIR reviewer why.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: inside a defined score band, tier decides order. One test with two concrete score pairs and one expected ordering each. The tier field and its citation are the observable acceptance evidence for that ordering, not an independent behavior — a tier value that never affects rank would satisfy no part of the need statement.

requirements.text: A candidate whose `acquisition_path_tier` is 1 carries a `far_7_107_1_order_exemption` flag set true with its citation, recording that an order under an existing indefinite-delivery vehicle whose base-contract consolidation was already justified requires no new FAR 7.107-2 determination; the flag is false on every candidate of tier 2 through 5.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-274** (CORE-274): Input: the TP-273 cluster, whose ranked candidates are `seaport-nxg` (tier 1) and `gsa-mas` (tier 2), plus one `NEW-VEHICLE-INDICATED` entry (tier 5). Expected: the `seaport-nxg` entry carries `far_7_107_1_order_exemption` = true with citation "FAR 7.107-1"; the `gsa-mas` and `NEW-VEHICLE-INDICATED` entries carry `far_7_107_1_order_exemption` = false.
requirements.rationale: FAR 7.107-1 is the specific legal reason the lowest friction tier is the shortest path: the consolidation determination has already been made and approved at the base contract, so the requirement owner does not restart a DASN(P) or HCA approval cycle under NMCARS 5207.107-2. That single fact is the most consequential piece of insight this tool can hand a NAVAIR requirement owner, and it is the difference between a recommendation that saves months and one that only reorders a list. Flagging it is assembling a citation, not making the determination — the determination itself stays with the SPE, CAO, DASN(P), or HCA.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: the exemption flag's value is a function of tier. Verified by one run over three candidates of tiers 1, 2 and 5 with one expected flag value each. Distinct from CORE-273, which asserts an ordering; a correct ordering with no exemption flag, or a flag with no effect on order, are different failures.

requirements.text: Every run's manifest records the `kb_version` string and the SHA-256 of the knowledge-base manifest file the run read, alongside the candidate list.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-275** (CORE-275): Run the pipeline once end-to-end on the N=20 reference set in an image carrying knowledge base `2026.09.1`. Expected: `manifest.json` contains `kb_version` = "2026.09.1" and `kb_manifest_sha256` equal to the SHA-256 of `kb/manifest.sha256` as shipped in that image, computed independently outside the container.
requirements.rationale: A vehicle recommendation is only reproducible against the knowledge base that produced it: ordering periods close, ceilings fill, and vehicles are re-competed, so the same input documents will legitimately yield a different answer six months later. Stamping the run with the knowledge base's version and digest is what lets a PGIL reviewer — or a protest record — reconstruct why a given candidate was returned on a given date. OUT-440 already requires one manifest indexing the bundle; it does not require these two fields.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: two identifying values appear in the run manifest. Verified by one run and one comparison against an independently computed digest. It asserts nothing about the knowledge base's own shape (KB-600) or whether the run verified it (KB-630).

requirements.text: Where a cluster's requirement content falls in a SeaPort-NxG Annex 22 functional area, SeaPort-NxG appears in the ranked candidate list, or the candidate record names the NMCARS 5237.102 exception category the cluster's documents evidence and cites the document span evidencing it.
requirements.test_procedure: **TP-276** (CORE-276): Input (a) a 3-document cluster of Navy engineering-services PWSs whose content maps to an Annex 22 functional area: expected, `seaport-nxg` appears somewhere in the ranked candidate list. Input (b) the same cluster with each document carrying an SF 1449 commercial-item cover page: expected, either `seaport-nxg` appears in the list, or the record carries `seaport_consideration_exception` = "FAR Part 12 commercial" with a (source filename, section path, sentence) span citing the SF 1449 text. Input (c) a cluster of NAVFAC construction documents: expected, neither the candidate nor the exception field is required to mention SeaPort-NxG.
requirements.rationale: NMCARS 5237.102 makes consideration of SeaPort mandatory for Annex 22 functional areas — not using it without a FAR 6.302 J&A requires a D&F to DASN(P) with HCA endorsement (5237.103). For Navy services work, "best available resource" is therefore not an open question the tool may answer purely on text similarity; the rule names the starting point. Encoding it as "present it, or name the exception the documents evidence" keeps the tool assembling evidence rather than concluding that an exception applies. SeaPort-NxG is also the single most likely member of PGIL's list of 20 for Navy services requirements, so silently dropping it costs scored points.
requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion with a two-branch expected output (vehicle present, or exception named with a citing span) driven by the same rule — this is the structure of the rule itself, not two behaviors; a reviewer cannot partially satisfy it, since failing to present SeaPort-NxG without a cited exception fails, and presenting it passes regardless of the exception field.
