requirements.atomicity_note: One assertion: one provenance block with three named fields, written by one writer and checked by one schema assertion — the same shape as DATA-IN-100's four-field normalized record, which the RTVM already treats as atomic.

derive.coverage_note: Three parts of this need statement are already covered and I am not restating them. (1) The existence of a reviewable per-run bundle that a government evaluator reads is OUT-440; NFR-540, NFR-550, NFR-570 and OUT-490 attach to that bundle rather than create a second one. (2) Document-level traceability already exists: DATA-OUT-300 requires each candidate to carry "the set of source documents that contributed to it," and VehicleRecommender.cs already emits ContributingDocuments. NFR-560 does not restate that — it refines it from filename granularity to a resolvable span or knowledge-base row, which is the granularity the need statement asks for ("back to a document span or a knowledge-base row"). (3) The no-LLM-in-core constraint that keeps the recommendation path deterministic and inspectable (CORE-240) already does part of the "never substitute for a determination" work, since an inspected, non-generative path cannot write determination prose; NFR-550 covers the remaining exposure, which is the optional LLM summarization step CORE-250 permits. Nothing in the current RTVM mentions small business, FAR Part 19, approval authority, decision-support labeling, or recommendation completeness — OUT-450 through OUT-490, NFR-540 and NFR-550 are genuinely new ground, and OUT-450/460/470/480 all refine DATA-OUT-300's result record rather than replacing it. One honest caveat on OUT-490: DATA-IN-110 already establishes the "flag it, don't drop it, and say why" pattern for skipped inputs; OUT-490 applies that same pattern to an under-evidenced recommendation, so it is a sibling of an existing idea rather than a new one, but DATA-IN-110 is about input files and says nothing about recommendation completeness.
derive.tensions:
Five real conflicts, none of them cosmetic.

1. Nothing in the codebase can populate these fields today, and OUT-490 will say so out loud. IngestionRunner.cs builds a DocumentRecord from four fields only (text, type, filename, date) — no PIID, PSC, NAICS, office code or section structure is extracted anywhere, DocumentTypeClassifier.cs returns Unknown for anything outside five literal tokens, and there is no vehicle or incumbent knowledge base in the repository at all. On the current build, every field OUT-450/460/470/480 asks for resolves to `unknown`, so OUT-490 marks every recommendation `incomplete`. That is the correct and honest outcome, but it means these requirements are blocked on two capabilities that no RTVM item yet covers: structured field extraction at ingest, and a vendored knowledge base. If the client wants them Approved rather than Blocked, those two predecessors need IDs of their own in the DATA-IN and CORE bands.

2. Incumbent business size and set-aside history do not live in the documents — they live in FPDS/USAspending/SAM.gov. NFR-500 and NFR-510 forbid fetching them at run time, so they must be vendored into the image, which makes them stale by construction (NFR-570's version stamp exists because of this) and adds weight against CORE-220's 30-minute, 1-core/2GB budget. A national incumbent-size table is large; the knowledge base will need to be scoped to the corpus or to Navy offices, and that scoping is itself a documented decision a judge may probe.

3. "Every consolidation recommendation" needs a definition the current code does not have. VehicleRecommender.cs maps one cluster to one candidate and scores singleton clusters 1.0 "by convention," which puts one-document clusters at the top of the ranked list. A one-document cluster is not a consolidation at all — there is nothing to consolidate — so a small-business impact note on it is meaningless. I have scoped OUT-450/460/470 to recommendations covering two or more member requirements, which means the ranking bug is now load-bearing for compliance, not just for precision@5: while singletons rank first, the top of the list carries no impact notes and OUT-490 marks it accordingly. Fixing the singleton scoring is a prerequisite to these requirements being worth anything.

4. NFR-550 can abort a run that CORE-250's optional LLM step poisoned. The core path cannot originate determination prose, but a summarization model can and will produce "necessary and justified" style sentences. I have written the gate as fail-the-run because a silently-stripped artifact is worse than a failed one, but the client should see the trade: a demo-day run could abort on a phrase the model chose. The alternative — drop the LLM artifact and finish the run — is defensible too and should be a deliberate client decision, not an implementation accident.

5. NFR-570's run timestamp puts a per-run-varying field in manifest.json, which CORE-210's reproducibility bar must not be read as forbidding. TP-210 compares the top-5 candidate list, not manifest bytes, so there is no conflict as written — but any future "diff the manifests" shortcut for CORE-210 or NFR-520 would break on the timestamp and on nothing else. Worth stating in the SDD before someone writes that test.

One boundary risk to flag rather than hide: OUT-480 has the tool name an approval authority, which is one step closer to acquisition-strategy reasoning than the other items. It is defensible only because the selection is a published lookup on two shown inputs (NMCARS 5207.107-2/-3 against estimated value and bundling indicator) with the thresholds held in the versioned knowledge base, and because the field says which determination the evidence would feed rather than that a determination is warranted. If it ever starts selecting on facts the tool estimated rather than extracted, it crosses the ai-boundaries.md line.

vet_partial.contradicts: DATA-OUT-300 (structural contradiction, not a resource/LLM/network one). DATA-OUT-300 defines "a ranked candidate contract-vehicle list **per run**, each candidate carrying a numeric confidence/score and the set of source documents that contributed to it." The code implements exactly that and no more: src/Naadap.Output/VehicleRecommender.cs does `clusters.Select(cluster => BuildCandidate(cluster, vectorsByFilename))` — one candidate per cluster, 1:1, its own XML doc comment saying "One cluster maps to exactly one candidate" — then flattens them into a single run-level ordering by (Score, ContributingDocuments.Count, VehicleId). CORE-280's phrase "the next-lower-ranked candidate in the same cluster's list" presupposes that each cluster owns a ranked list of MULTIPLE candidate vehicles. No approved requirement establishes that cardinality, and the code does not have it. CORE-280 therefore smuggles a structural redefinition of DATA-OUT-300 (one-candidate-per-cluster becomes many-candidates-per-cluster) into a subordinate clause of a requirement nominally about arithmetic. That change is real and probably right — it is what a vehicle knowledge base implies — but it needs its own RTVM row and its own approval, not to arrive as a presupposition. Claiming `refines_existing: DATA-OUT-300` is not enough: a refinement narrows or sharpens; this changes the cardinality of the record. Secondary: CORE-280 also depends on CORE-286, which does not exist in the RTVM. The RTVM's own header rule is "Don't enter line items against a [PROPOSED] item ... wait for it to become [CONFIRMED]"; the same discipline applies to an intra-RTVM forward dependency. Both the requirement text and TP-280's input set ("run with the abstention floor F = 0.400") are unresolvable until CORE-286 lands. No contradiction with CORE-240 (no LLM), NFR-510 (no egress), CORE-220/NFR-530 (one subtraction per candidate), or CORE-210 (double subtraction of deterministic inputs is deterministic) — I checked those and it is clean on all four.
vet_partial.atomicity_problem: Split at the piecewise boundary. The text defines one field by two rules with different inputs, different failure modes, and different verification dependencies: (a) interior ranks, margin = score(i) - score(i+1), a pure function of the candidate list, testable today with nothing configured; (b) the lowest rank, margin = score(n) - F, a function of the list AND an externally configured abstention floor owned by a requirement that does not exist. A reviewer can fully satisfy (a) and wholly fail (b) — ship correct interior gaps and emit null, 0.0, or score(n) itself at the tail — and the requirement is half-met. That is the "could a reviewer partially satisfy it" test failing. (b) also cannot enter Test status until CORE-286 fixes F's value, units, and whether it is a build constant or a per-run parameter; leaving them fused means (a) sits Blocked behind (b) for no reason. Split into CORE-280 (interior adjacent-rank gap) and CORE-280B (tail gap against the CORE-286 floor, Status: Blocked on CORE-286). Note this is a genuine split, not pedantry: I considered and rejected the argument that a piecewise definition of a single value is one assertion, because the two branches do not share an input set.
vet_partial.verifiability_problem:
Three distinct reasons the stated method cannot yield pass/fail as written.

1. The TP's "input" is not an input. TP-280 says "Input: a document set constructed to produce one cluster with four candidate vehicles scored 0.810, 0.790, 0.520 and 0.510." Those are outputs of the stage under test, stated as a precondition. Nobody can author a corpus of SOW/PWS text that drives a TF-IDF-cosine pipeline to four scores exact to three decimal places; you would be back-solving a black box. Compare the existing rows, which specify real inputs and leave outputs to the expectation: TP-100 ("6 documents ... 2 SOW, 1 PWS, 1 CDRL, 1 sources-sought notice, 1 open-source text sample, in a mix of PDF and DOCX"), TP-200 ("a synthetic 10-document set constructed so that documents {A, C, E} share one requirement theme ... with {F..J} as unrelated distractors"). TP-280 is in neither form. The honest procedure is a component-level Test that feeds a fixed in-memory/serialized candidate list to the annotation step — which is legitimate and should simply say so.

2. The input premise is unconstructible under the current record model regardless of precision. A cluster today yields exactly one candidate (VehicleRecommender.BuildCandidate), so "one cluster with four candidate vehicles" cannot be produced by any document set. Further, the `Score` those candidates carry is `ComputeCohesion` — mean pairwise cosine among the cluster's own member documents — not a cluster-to-vehicle match score, and there is no vehicle knowledge base anywhere in the codebase to score against. So the numbers in the TP are not just hard to hit, they are not the same quantity the requirement is about.

3. The field is undefined at exactly the condition this block exists to detect. "The next-lower-ranked candidate" has no referent when two candidates carry equal scores — and a flat distribution with ties is the limiting case of the grey area the need statement describes. The requirement meant to measure flatness goes undefined at maximal flatness. The existing code does impose a total order (Score, then ContributingDocuments.Count, then VehicleId ordinal), so the fix is cheap, but the requirement must say "the candidate at the next position in the ranked order" and state that equal scores yield 0.000 — otherwise an implementer may legitimately emit null, and the test cannot adjudicate.

4. Reconstructability defect, which is the one that actually undercuts the stated rationale. The requirement does not say which scores the difference is taken over. ResultVisualizationWriter.cs renders scores with `{candidate.Score:0.000}`. If the margin is computed on full-precision doubles while the record shows rounded scores, then at internal scores 0.8104 and 0.7896 the record reads "0.810, 0.790, margin 0.021" — a figure a reviewer cannot derive from the record in front of them. The rationale invokes ai-boundaries rule 3 ("the record must be reconstructable"); as written the requirement permits violating it. Pin the arithmetic to the scores *as recorded*.
vet_partial.test_procedure_problem: Beyond the unconstructible input (above): (a) The expected output bundles a second assertion — "in the same rank order as the score field" — onto a value check. Worse, read literally it is false on its own numbers: the margins 0.020, 0.270, 0.010, 0.110 are not in rank order of anything. If the intent is "records appear in score-rank order," that is already DATA-OUT-300/TP-300 territory and does not belong here; delete the clause. (b) The TP conspicuously omits the tie case (two equal scores), which is the single most important case for a flatness metric and the one an implementer is most likely to get wrong. (c) "each within 1e-9 of the stated value" is fine as a float tolerance (0.810-0.790 in IEEE-754 double is 0.020000000000000018, comfortably inside), but it is the wrong assertion once the reconstructability fix lands — the test should assert the field equals the difference of the two *serialized* score values, which is an exact comparison. (d) The arithmetic in the proposed TP is correct (0.020 / 0.270 / 0.010 / 0.110 against F=0.400) — I verified all four; the problem is the premise and the bundling, not the sums.
vet_partial.domain_error: The source citation is misapplied, which under references/ai-boundaries.md's own "Citations" rule ("Never fabricate a clause number, a threshold, a vehicle name") is the kind of defect this project holds itself to. The requirement cites vehicle-matching.md's "Output record" section for the proposition "every recommendation traces to a row or span." That sentence is real — "Everything in the record traces to a knowledge-base row or a document span" — but it establishes *provenance of claims to sources*, and a derived arithmetic gap between two scores traces to neither a KB row nor a document span. The same section's schema lists `score` inside `candidate_vehicles` and contains no margin field at all, so it does not support recording one. ai-boundaries rule 3 is stretched the same way: it calls for "knowledge-base version, model hashes, and run timestamp on every output," not for confidence-spread fields. The correct citation, which supports the requirement squarely, is vehicle-matching.md, "The shape of the problem": "The output must let a contracting officer see why, because a bare score cannot be defended in a determination or a debrief." Use that. Separately, the field name "decision margin" is a poor choice in this domain: ai-boundaries.md's whole line is that the tool assembles and never originates a decision, and a field a CO reads that is literally named for a decision invites the reading that the number carries decision weight. Name it for the arithmetic — `adjacent_rank_gap` or `score_gap` — which costs nothing and does not have to be walked back in a debrief. "Abstention floor" is an ML reject-option term, not an acquisition term of art; that is acceptable as internal vocabulary but should be defined once in CORE-286 rather than assumed.
vet_partial.scope_creep_reason: Confined to the second clause, and mild — I am not inflating this. The interior adjacent-rank gap is genuinely implied by the need statement: "flat" is not actionable until it is measured, and the rationale says so correctly. But anchoring the lowest-ranked candidate's margin to an abstention floor presupposes that the system abstains — a behavioral design choice that no confirmed stakeholder need and no approved RTVM row has adopted. The need statement asks "when the distribution is flat, which way should the recommender go?"; abstention is one candidate answer among several (widen the list, fall back to office affinity, surface the tie to the human). CORE-280 cannot be implemented without adopting that answer, so approving CORE-280 as written silently approves abstention. Splitting off CORE-280B and blocking it on CORE-286 confines the decision to where it belongs. Also flagging the trace: CORE-280 claims SN-1 and SN-6. SN-6 (analysis transparency) is exactly right. SN-1 is judges/accuracy/top-5-in-30-minutes, and recording a gap field changes no prediction and moves no score — it cannot affect the 2-points-per-correct-prediction rubric on its own. Drop SN-1; it belongs on whichever of CORE-281/282/288 actually conditions the ranking on the gap.
vet_partial.recommended_text: CORE-280 | Each candidate at position i of a cluster's ranked candidate-vehicle list, where a position i+1 exists in that list, carries a numeric adjacent-rank gap field equal to that candidate's score minus the score of the candidate at position i+1, computed from the score values as serialized in the DATA-OUT-300 record so that the gap is reconstructable from the record alone. Ranking is a total order; where two adjacent candidates carry equal scores the gap is 0. | SN-6 | Test | Draft || CORE-280B | The candidate at the final position of a cluster's ranked candidate-vehicle list carries the same adjacent-rank gap field, equal to its serialized score minus the abstention floor defined by CORE-286. | SN-6 | Test | Blocked (on CORE-286) || PREREQUISITE ROW, must be proposed and approved before either of the above — neither DATA-OUT-300 nor the current code gives a cluster more than one candidate vehicle: DATA-OUT-nnn | Each cluster in the run's result record carries its own ranked list of one or more candidate contract vehicles drawn from the vehicle knowledge base, replacing DATA-OUT-300's one-candidate-per-cluster mapping. | SN-1, SN-6 | Test | Draft || TP-280 (CORE-280): Input: a fixed DATA-OUT-300 result record for one cluster, written at the pipeline's output precision, whose candidate list holds four vehicles with scores 0.810, 0.790, 0.790 and 0.510, passed to the gap-annotation step. Expected: the serialized candidate records at positions 1, 2 and 3 carry adjacent-rank gap values of exactly 0.020, 0.000 and 0.280, each exactly equal to the difference of the two serialized score values at the corresponding positions; the position-4 record is out of scope for this procedure (see TP-280B). || TP-280B (CORE-280B): Input: the TP-280 record, run with the CORE-286 abstention floor F = 0.400. Expected: the position-4 candidate record carries an adjacent-rank gap of exactly 0.110, equal to its serialized score 0.510 minus F. || Corrected source citation for both: .claude/skills/gov-acquisition-sme/references/vehicle-matching.md, "The shape of the problem" — "The output must let a contracting officer see why, because a bare score cannot be defended in a determination or a debrief."
vet_partial.reasoning:
The idea survives; this drafting of it does not. What survives: the gap between adjacent ranks is a real, cheap, deterministic measurement, it is genuinely implied by the need statement (you cannot act on "flat" before you measure flat), it does not duplicate any existing row — DATA-OUT-300 gives each candidate a score and its contributing documents and nothing else — and it is clean against every hard constraint I checked: no LLM (CORE-240), no egress (NFR-510), negligible against 1c/2GB in 30 min (CORE-220) and the 8c/16GB ceiling (NFR-530), and a subtraction of deterministic inputs cannot perturb CORE-210's top-5 identity. It is also not invented: the rationale's point that a top-1 at 0.81 with a 0.20 gap and a top-1 at 0.81 with a 0.002 gap are different claims is correct, and today's record genuinely cannot tell them apart.

What fails: four things, any one of which blocks approval.

First and worst, the requirement presupposes a record structure that neither DATA-OUT-300 nor the code has. "The next-lower-ranked candidate in the same cluster's list" only means something if a cluster owns a list of several candidate vehicles. VehicleRecommender.cs maps one cluster to exactly one candidate and the run holds one flat ranking; its own doc comment says "One cluster maps to exactly one candidate." So the structural change rides in as a presupposition inside a requirement about arithmetic. That is how RTVMs rot. It needs its own row.

Second, the test procedure is not executable and is not in the house style. Its stated input is a set of four output scores to three decimals; no document set can be authored to produce those, and under the present 1:1 model no document set can produce four candidates in one cluster at all. The scores in question are also the wrong quantity — `Score` today is ComputeCohesion, mean pairwise cosine among the cluster's own members, not a vehicle-match score, and there is no vehicle KB to match against. TP-100 and TP-200 specify documents and let the expectation carry the numbers; TP-280 inverts that. Recast it as a component-level Test over a fixed serialized candidate list, which is honest and runs today.

Third, the field is undefined precisely where it matters. On equal scores there is no "next-lower-ranked" candidate, and ties are the limit case of the flat distribution this whole block exists to detect. The metric for flatness goes undefined at maximum flatness. Cheap to fix — the code already has a total tie-break chain — but the requirement has to say it, and the TP has to exercise it, which is why my replacement TP uses 0.810/0.790/0.790/0.510 rather than four distinct scores.

Fourth, the requirement does not pin which scores the difference is over, and ResultVisualizationWriter renders scores at `0.000`. Full-precision margin against rounded displayed scores gives a reviewer a number they cannot derive from the record — which defeats the rationale's own appeal to ai-boundaries rule 3. Pin it to the serialized values.

Two smaller items I am not willing to wave through. The citation is aimed at a sentence about provenance of claims to KB rows and document spans; a derived arithmetic gap traces to neither, and the cited schema has no margin field. The correct support is one section earlier, "a bare score cannot be defended in a determination or a debrief" — which is a better argument for the requirement anyway. And "decision margin" is the wrong name in a domain whose governing rule is that the tool never originates a decision; name the field after the arithmetic.

On atomicity I considered arguing the other way — a piecewise definition of a single value is arguably one assertion — and rejected it, because the two branches do not share an input set. Interior gaps need only the candidate list; the tail gap needs a configured floor from a requirement that does not exist. An implementer can pass one and fail the other, and fusing them parks a testable-today requirement behind an unwritten one. Hence SPLIT rather than REWRITE, with the rewrite folded into the split pieces.

vet_partial.atomicity_problem: The text carries two independently testable assertions and fails the "could a reviewer partially satisfy it" test. Assertion (a), sentence 1: the MEMBERSHIP RULE — the group is rank-1 plus every candidate within ε of the rank-1 score. Assertion (b), sentence 2: the EMISSION RULE — the group is present on the result record in every case, including the one-member case. An implementation can compute (a) perfectly and still fail (b) by omitting or nulling the field when the group is a singleton; that is textbook partial satisfaction. The atomicity_note's defense ("one assertion: membership of a named set") is wrong on its face: sentence 2 is not about membership, it is about presence, and its normative content ("in every case, including when it has exactly one member") is a separate defect class that sentence 1 does not constrain. The proof that this is two requirements is in the author's own TP: TP-281 exercises only (a) — its expected output is a three-member group — and never exercises the singleton case (b) claims to require. A requirement whose own test procedure covers half its text is not atomic. The two halves also belong in different RTVM categories: (a) is computation (CORE 200-299), (b) is internal result representation (DATA-OUT 300-399, the block DATA-OUT-300 already owns). Split as given in recommended_text.
vet_partial.verifiability_problem: Three separate reasons the stated method (Test) cannot yield a defensible pass/fail as written. (1) The comparator is undefined in the requirement text. "Within the documented near-tie epsilon (ε) of the highest score" does not say whether a candidate exactly ε below rank-1 is in or out. The TP's parenthetical arithmetic silently assumes "≤ ε", but a TP may not define the requirement it tests. Four domain errors, one of them disqualifying.

1. "Annex 22-eligible" is a category error, and it makes rung 1 inert. NMCARS 5237.102 is cited correctly as far as it goes (far-consolidation-rules.md: "SeaPort consideration is mandatory for Annex 22 functional areas"), but Annex 22 is a list of functional areas describing the REQUIREMENT — Engineering Services and Program Management Services — not a property a candidate vehicle can hold. The fixture says "none of them Annex 22-eligible (key 1 neutral for all three)," which is not a coherent statement about vehicles. Worse, when the rule does fire it names exactly one vehicle, SeaPort-NxG, so rung 1 can only ever be neutral or promote a single hard-coded vehicle; it can never order two other candidates relative to each other. A rung with that shape is not a tie-break key at all, it is a presence-and-address flag.

2. Mandatory CONSIDERATION is being encoded as mandatory PREFERENCE. NMCARS 5237.102 requires that SeaPort be considered, and 5237.103 requires a D&F to DASN(P) with HCA endorsement if it is considered and not used. The correct machine encoding is "SeaPort-NxG appears in the candidate set for an Annex 22 cluster and the record carries the 5237.103 D&F checklist items" — not "SeaPort outranks." And the rule's own exception list (FAR 6.302 actions, below SAT, 8(a) set-asides, FAR Part 12/8.4 commercial, Part 13 simplified) means the tool cannot even determine whether the rule applies without first settling commerciality and set-aside status — both reserved decisions under ai-boundaries.md. Rung 1 therefore either assumes a reserved determination or silently ignores the exceptions.

3. The ordering-period rung is contracting-wrong twice. First, what has to be true is that the ORDER is placed inside the ordering period, not that the ordering period spans the whole performance period; under FAR 16.505 and 52.216-22 performance routinely runs past the ordering period on an order issued before it closed. A vehicle with 400 days of ordering period left is fully usable for an award next quarter, and ranking it below a 1200-day vehicle for that reason is a discriminator no CO would recognize or write into a file. Second, per point above, ordering period is a hard constraint in this project's own design, not a preference — if V-B's headroom genuinely fails against the cluster POP it should be removed and there is no three-way tie group at all; if it passes, headroom carries no further signal. The fixture is incoherent either way. The far-consolidation-rules.md line the proposal is leaning on ("Check scope, ceiling remaining, ordering period against the intended period of performance, NAICS pool, and set-aside status of the pool") is a screening checklist, not a ranking key.

4. "Friction rank per the vehicle taxonomy" misreads the cited section. The section title is quoted accurately, but "Vehicle taxonomy by friction, lowest first" is a taxonomy of ACQUISITION APPROACHES, not of vehicles — rung 4 is "New agency IDIQ" and rung 5 is "New stand-alone contract," neither of which is a candidate vehicle. Applied to vehicles it collapses to three levels (agency MAC / FSS-MAS / GWAC-other-agency) and, in collapsing, it drops the two real sourced discriminators in that file: DFARS 217.770's documented best-interest review before using any non-DoD vehicle above SAT ("a legitimate recommendation for a Navy requirement but never a free one") and the DON Best Practices Handbook FY2024 rule that "tiered DON contracts shall have priority consideration" over other agencies' tiered contracts. Those belong above a statistical office-usage prior, not at rung 4 beneath it.

5. The legal consequence the ladder ignores entirely is small business. There is no socioeconomic rung anywhere. Between two otherwise-tied vehicles, the choice of vehicle decides whether an order-level set-aside is even available (FAR 19.504; 13 CFR 125.2(e), which says the CO "must set-aside a Multiple Award Contract if the requirements for a set-aside are met"; SeaPort-NxG determines size at order level; NAWCTSD FTSS V has 2 SB primes against 7 unrestricted; the NAVAIR PM CSS MAC is an SB MAC). Breaking the tie toward whatever the office historically used institutionalizes incumbency at precisely the point where the rule of two (FAR 19.502-2) and the set-aside-preserving structures (19.502-3, 19.502-4, 19.504) are still live options. Note the terminology trap the ladder would walk a reviewer into: 19.502-4 reserves and 19.502-2 set-asides are different instruments with different triggers, and a tool that silently ranks past both while emitting a NMCARS citation as its stated reason will read, to the SPE or DASN(P) reviewing the resulting determination, as the tool having taken a Part 19 position it has no authority to take.

Nothing invented on dollar figures — the requirement cites no thresholds, which is to its credit; the $2M / $8M / 10%-or-5%-or-$9.4M figures it could have gotten wrong are all absent.

The instinct is right and the need statement is real — a flat distribution has to break somewhere, and an undisclosed break is indefensible. The proposal fails on what it puts in the ladder, not on whether there should be one.

Structurally it is two requirements wearing one row: the ordering rule and the disclosure field are independently implementable, independently breakable, and verified by different methods (Test for the fixture ordering, Inspection for "documented"). It also leaves refines_existing empty when it plainly refines two live rows: CORE-210, because the ladder's terminal rung is the mechanism that makes "identical top-5 in >=95% of runs" reachable at all, and DATA-OUT-300, because adding a named field to the per-candidate record is a change to that record's definition. Listing DATA-OUT-300 only under depends_on hides that from the traceability matrix.

On domain, three of the five rungs are wrong in ways a contracting officer would catch on first read. Rung 1 treats Annex 22 as a property of a vehicle when it is a description of the requirement's functional area, which makes the rung inert for ordering any two non-SeaPort candidates, and it converts a procedural duty to consider into a ranking preference — the actual consequence of not using SeaPort is a 5237.103 D&F to DASN(P) with HCA endorsement, which is a document the tool should be assembling evidence for, not a thumb on a scale. Rung 3 contradicts the project's own stated rule that a failed constraint removes a vehicle rather than lowering it, and rests on the belief that the ordering period must span the period of performance, which is not how IDIQ ordering works. Rung 4 mis-cites a taxonomy of acquisition approaches as a taxonomy of vehicles and, in doing so, drops DFARS 217.770 and the DON-tiered-priority rule, the two discriminators in that file that a Navy CO would actually recognize.

The disqualifying one is rung 2. Office affinity is a fine scoring channel — vehicle-matching.md lists it as one — but promoting it to second place in a decision ladder makes "the office used it before" the near-universal tie-breaker, which is incumbency by construction at exactly the moment when the vehicle choice still determines whether an order-level set-aside is possible. ai-boundaries.md already names this failure mode: historical shares are descriptive, never automatic thresholds. The rationale's claim that naming the key keeps the tool on the assembling side of the line actually inverts under rung 1: attaching a NMCARS citation to a machine-produced ordering makes it read, in the file, as the tool having taken a policy position. The fix is the disposition field in the third split piece, not the key name alone.

The test procedure would not catch any of this, and would not catch a reversed ladder either — it contains no pair where two rungs disagree, never reaches the terminal rung that CORE-210 depends on, omits the cluster POP that rung 3 is defined against, and gives no expected value for the top candidate's disclosure field.

Not a duplicate of anything in the RTVM; no invented citations or dollar figures. Worth keeping as a concept, in three rows, with the ladder rebuilt.
